citations.title: AI Overview
excerpts: The following terms are used throughout this document:

• **Model** : A large language model: software trained on large amounts of text to understand and generate language. The models used by Formalize are pre-trained, general-purpose models developed by Anthropic.
• **Prompt** : The input sent to the model for a single request - for example, the documents and field definitions SmartFill reads, or the records and instructions Formalize IQ works from.
• **Completion** : The output the model returns for a prompt - for example, SmartFill’s sug- gested values, or Formalize IQ’s answer or proposed action.
• **Inference** : The act of running a model on a prompt to produce a completion. Inference is stateless: the model does not remember anything between requests.
• **General-purpose AI model** : An AI model capable of performing a wide range of tasks, as defined in the EU AI Act. The Claude models used by Formalize are general-purpose AI models.

• **Amazon Bedrock** : An AWS-managed service that runs AI models from multiple devel- opers entirely within AWS infrastructure. The model developer has no access to the data processed by the service.
• **Agent** : An AI capability that completes multi-step tasks by calling well-defined tools, always bound by the requesting user’s permissions. Formalize IQ is built on agents.

• **Tool** : A well-defined, single-purpose function an agent can call - for example, to look up records the user has access to or to draft a new record. Every tool call is checked against the requesting user’s permissions, and tools that change data additionally require the user’s approval.

• **Sandbox** : An isolated, temporary computing environment in which an agent can run code, with no route to the public internet, to our network, or to the platform. Formalize uses a sandbox that is provided and operated by AWS.

• **Prompt injection** : An attack in which instructions are hidden inside content an AI reads - a document, a web page, a form answer - in an attempt to make it act against the user’s intent. The safeguards against it are described under Formalize IQ.
The table below summarises the key facts and controls described in this document:
**Capabilities** SmartFill (assisted form-filling) and Formalize IQ (a governed AI assistant / agent)
**AI models** Anthropic Claude, accessed through Amazon Bedrock (an AWS-managed service)

All AI inference is performed through Amazon Bedrock, an AWS-managed service that runs Anthropic’s Claude models entirely within AWS infrastructure. Our backend communicates di- rectly with Amazon Bedrock, and customer data is never sent to the model provider (Anthropic) or to any other third party:

• Model invocations use Amazon Bedrock EU inference profiles, which guarantee that AI processing happens exclusively within AWS regions located in the EU. No data is trans- ferred outside the EU/EEA in connection with the AI capabilities.

• Amazon Bedrock operates the models entirely within AWS. Using the AI capabilities therefore does not introduce any new sub-processor: the processing is performed by AWS, which already hosts the platform and is covered by our data processing agreement and sub-processor list. The model provider has no access to requests or responses.

• Two Formalize IQ capabilities use AWS-managed tooling alongside the models, and both stay inside AWS. Code execution runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore’s code interpreter in Frankfurt (eu-central-1), the same region as the rest of the platform. Web search runs through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore’s managed web search service in Ireland (eu-west- 1), the EU region in which AWS offers it: searches are answered from a web index that Amazon operates itself, and pages the agent opens are served from Amazon’s cache of the web, so no request is handed to a third-party search engine and our infrastructure never opens a connection to the public internet. AWS offers a mode in which pages missing from the cache are fetched from the external web; we keep it disabled. All of
these are AWS services used under the same agreement as the rest of our AWS usage, so none of them introduces a new sub-processor.
• All communication with Amazon Bedrock, including the AWS tooling described above, is TLS encrypted and authenticated with AWS credentials, just like all other internal service communication.
